item.title: Listen: Bristol Unpacked with police and crime commissioner Clare Moody on fixing force culture, and the government axing her role
item.description: Just 18 months into her term, the Labour politician in charge of police scrutiny in Avon and Somerset has, along with peers across the country, been told she represents a 'failed experiment' that will end in 2028. Neil asks Clare Moody how that feels, and what she aims to achieve while still in office. The post Listen: Bristol Unpacked with police and crime commissioner Clare Moody on fixing force culture, and the government axing her role appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Hurt people, hurt people: The hidden lives of children behind bars
item.description: At 10 years old, England and Wales has one of the lowest ages of criminal responsibility in the world. Here we offer a glimpse into child incarceration, the school to prison pipeline and stalling youth justice system reforms. Starting here, on the outskirts of Bristol... The post Hurt people, hurt people: The hidden lives of children behind bars appeared first on The Bristol Cable.

item.title: Listen: Bristol Unpacked with Green councillor Ani Townsend on art, inequality and the case for a universal basic income
item.description: Should the state give people free money? This week Ani and Neil discuss how a universal basic income would work, why supporting the arts is a class issue, and whether ‘eco-populist’ Green leader Zack Polanski can take on the traditional parties – and Reform.
